messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content: At a pressure of 10 kPa (about one‑tenth of an atmosphere), pure water freezes at roughly **–2 °C**. This is slightly below the normal 0 °C freezing point at 101.3 kPa because the solid–liquid equilibrium line for water slopes downward as pressure decreases toward the triple point.
